chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abbas ibn Amir from Ali ibn Ma'mar from Khalid al-Qalanisi said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man brings me a garment, so I display it, and when I am given something for it, I add to it and take it. He said: 'Do not add to it.' I said: 'Why?' He said: 'Is it not that when you display it, you love to be given more than its price?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do not add to it.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَعْرِضُهُ: I display it (showing the item to potential buyers)
key_terms.زِدْتُ فِيهِ: I added to it (increasing the price or value)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on inflating prices when displaying goods for sale?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *al-istiqra'* (displaying goods for sale) by instructing the seller not to inflate the price after the item has been presented, citing the psychological bias where sellers naturally desire a higher return for their displayed wares. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on removing *gharar* (uncertainty/deception) in transactions by aligning the final price with the true value perceived during the display, ensuring fairness and preventing subtle exploitation of the buyer's trust.
